gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, on the makers' own US stores on 2026-11-14, a front-plus-rear dash-cam CarPlay screen costs $129.99 (ESSGOO E64) or $139.99 (Lamtto RC28, 64 GB card included), against $249.99 for the dual-camera Carpuride W903 that ChatGPT picked, and that $219.99 buys a W903 with only the front camera.
standout_why: I compared against rottenwifi.com and carcody.com, which have the same table, and motorys.com, all opened 2026-11-14. Rottenwifi and carcody already give the W903 at $219.99 for the front camera and $249.99 for both cameras. They also list the IIWEY iK7 at $139.99 and say its rear camera only switches on in reverse. Neither prices the ESSGOO E64, the Lamtto RC28 or the W903S at the maker's store. Motorys gives no prices for any model with a dash cam. I could not read the cited Road & Track page or Car and Driver (the fetch tool can't reach those sites) or the DashGear Lab pages (TLS error). DashGear Lab has an RC28 review and a list of screens under $150, so it may already have the RC28 price. That is why this is a 1 and not a 2.
decides: It confirms the W903 as the top pick only for a shopper who pays $249.99 for the dual-camera kit. ChatGPT's card showed $242.99 next to '4K front + 1080p rear', and the $219.99 W903 has no rear camera. For a budget around $150, ESSGOO's maker store has the E64 with dual cameras at $129.99 and Lamtto's has the RC28 at $139.99, both about $110 to $120 under the W903 dual kit. That makes the $100 to $200 budget button a real choice and not just Rexing. For a camera on the back seat, the W903S at $279.90 adds an infrared 1080p cabin camera and comes with a 64 GB card.
